nt: The phrase **all of his house** could mean: (1) all the adult sons who could reasonably have succeeded Saul as king. In that case, **house** would mean “dynasty.” The author of 1 Chronicles does not describe the civil war between David and Saul’s youngest son Ish-bosheth (whom he calls Esh Baal in [9:49](../09/49.md)). Instead, he proceeds directly to the story of how the Israelites asked David to be their king at the end of that civil war. From his perspective, Saul’s dynasty effectively ended when he and his adult sons died in this battle. Alternate translation: [and his three adult sons who could have succeeded him as king died with him] or (2) as a generalization, all of the Israelite soldiers who were fighting together with Saul, that is, his sons and his bodyguard. That is the meaning of the similar phrase “all his men” in the parallel passage in [1 Samuel 31:6](../1sa/31/06.md). Alternate translation: [and three of his sons and all of his bodyguard died together]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [because of the sin that he committed against Yahweh]

The author is speaking as if the **word** of Yahweh (that is, a command that Yahweh spoke to Saul) were an object that Saul could have kept somewhere. To describe this aspect of Saul’s **transgression**, he is referring to the episode related in [1 Samuel 15:1–29](../1sa/15/01.md), in which Saul disobeys a direct command of Yahweh and the prophet Samuel tells him that Yahweh will make someone else the king of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, and you could refer your readers to the passage in 1 Samuel in a footnote. Alternate translation: [because of the command of Yahweh that he did not obey]

To describe this further aspect of Saul’s **transgression**, the author is referring to the episode related in [1 Samuel 26:3–19](../1sa/28/03.md), in which Saul goes to a medium for guidance and Samuel tells him that because of his disobedience, he is going to die in battle the next day. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could refer them to this passage in 1 Samuel in a footnote.
